findings: [P2] packages/cadenda/staging.py:prepare — Bound artifacts are ordered by artifact_id, whose review suffix is random, but reports[-1] is treated as the latest review. After a second successful review of the same run, staging can select the older report and reject valid current requirements. Select the report associated with the latest completed review using recorded event order, and test repeated reviews with deliberately reversed lexical IDs.

[P2] packages/cadenda/staging.py:apply — Requirements are rechecked before publication, but the final transaction checks only configuration and approval/run state. Recorder.flush holds a compatible shared maintenance lock and sends Beads comments outside SQLite transactions, so it can change requirement sources after the final prepare() and before release.rename(target). Publication then succeeds with stale requirement hashes. Serialize publication with Cadenda requirement writers through the final requirement check and rename; add a concurrency test injecting an Outbox delivery in this interval.
